note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: Samsung forecasts record third-quarter profit of $80 billion as AI boom fuels chip demand
items.blurb: Samsung's preliminary quarterly operating profit passed 100 trillion won for the first time, up 782% in a year on AI chip demand.

items.title: TSMC's September sales surge year-over-year as AI drives chip demand
items.blurb: September revenue rose 54.6% from a year earlier to about $16 billion, slightly below August's record, as AI chip orders held.

items.title: AI breakthroughs in robotics won't change your life any time soon
items.blurb: Roboticists say current AI models fail outside controlled settings, leaving useful home humanoids roughly a decade away.

items.title: Republican megadonors dominate 2026 midterm election as crypto and AI money surges, CNBC analysis finds
items.blurb: Crypto, AI and online gambling donors have put more than $377 million into the 2026 midterms, mostly behind Republicans.

items.title: OpenAI's math breakthrough points beyond math
items.blurb: OpenAI released 722 manuscripts of findings on long-standing math problems, drawing both excitement and unease from mathematicians.

items.title: Data centers face a sweeping new power regime
items.blurb: Lawmakers are weighing new costs and limits on data centers while speeding up the energy infrastructure that powers AI.

items.title: Women don't like AI. They have reasons
items.blurb: A Morgan Stanley survey finds women far more negative about AI than men, citing jobs, safety risks and data centers.

items.title: Amazon overhauls aging devices lineup with higher-priced Alexa tablet, dumping the budget Fire
items.blurb: Amazon replaced its budget Fire tablets with Alexa-branded models built around AI features, priced from $230 to $550.

items.title: Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave and other AI stocks sink on OpenAI revenue report
items.blurb: OpenAI told investors annualized revenue was about $50 billion, below the $68 billion widely reported, and AI stocks fell.

items.title: Trump: Anyone saying "AI" is "THE ENEMY!" The White House uses it
items.blurb: Trump pressed his order favoring the term "super intelligence" over "AI", though the order carries no penalty.

items.title: Cybersecurity stocks dip on Anthropic 'Cyber Mission' announcement
items.blurb: Security company shares slipped after Anthropic announced a new program aimed at defending critical systems with its models.

items.title: Axios Live: Americans don't have to accept AI risk, policymaker says
items.blurb: Rep. Sam Liccardo called the trade between AI progress and safety a false choice; business leaders urged stronger oversight.

items.title: Will AI scoop your science? Some researchers see a gloomy future
items.blurb: Scientists report AI companies answering their research questions first, raising worries about who gets credit for discoveries.

items.title: Google ordered to halt work on two data centers in 'Texas of Europe'
items.blurb: Finnish regulators told Google to pause two data center projects by Oct 23 until environmental reviews are complete.

items.title: CNBC Daily Open: AI rally defies bond market rout
items.blurb: AI chip stocks carried the S&P 500 to a record close while Temasek warned an AI reversal is the market's biggest risk.

items.title: Trillions are being 'wasted' on the AI boom, Arthur Hayes says. He's betting on what comes next
items.blurb: The former BitMEX chief argues data-center spending will end in overcapacity and a crash, adding to investor doubts about the buildout.

items.title: Common Sense Media rates ChatGPT a safety risk for teens
items.blurb: Testers found parent-linked accounts received no alerts during hour-long conversations about self-harm and suicide.

items.title: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
items.blurb: A method converts existing language models to read raw bytes, improving character-level reasoning while keeping practical speeds.

items.title: Anthropic unveils a new, cheaper Haiku model
items.blurb: Anthropic's smallest model arrives at a fraction of its predecessor's price, pressing the cost race among low-end AI models.

items.title: Microsoft to sell $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra containing Nvidia AI chip
items.blurb: Microsoft and Nvidia are betting buyers will pay a premium to run demanding AI work on a laptop instead of the cloud.

items.title: Microsoft looks to reboot the AI PC with Nvidia
items.blurb: Microsoft is carving out a high-end laptop category for local AI, and Meta plans to bring its Muse agent to Windows.

items.title: IMF paper warns of hedge fund risks
items.blurb: An IMF paper flags hedge funds' heavy use of borrowed money in AI stocks as a risk to financial stability.

items.title: U.S. government, Google join Zuckerberg-backed Biohub in $1.8 billion push for AI biology data
items.blurb: Washington, Alphabet and Meta back open datasets for training biology models, lifting the nonprofit effort to $1.8 billion.

items.title: Meta needs Muse to become more than an AI novelty
items.blurb: Meta's personal agent tops app charts and lifted the stock, but keeping users after the novelty fades is the test.
